traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Chrysobalanaceae: leaves alternate; leaves simple; veins pinnate; stipules present; plants hermaphrodite or polygamous; ovary superior; floral cup present; stems woody; flowers solitary, in cymes or in racemes; flowers zygomorphic; perianth usually sepals and petals, rarely tepals; fruit drupe; stamens (2-) 8 to 30 (-300); carpels 1 to 3. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.
